categories.main_business_segments: FactSet operates through three geographic segments: Americas (64% of revenues), EMEA (26%), and Asia Pacific (10%). Within each segment, the company organizes by firm type: Institutional Buyside, Dealmakers, Wealth, and Partnerships/CGS. The company provides multi-asset class financial data, analytics, and technology solutions to investment professionals including asset managers, bankers, wealth managers, hedge funds, and private equity professionals.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FactSet's core technology includes a configurable desktop and mobile platform, comprehensive data feeds, cloud-based digital solutions, and APIs. The company operates a hybrid cloud infrastructure with two fully redundant U.S. data centers and partnerships with multiple cloud providers. Key production methods involve aggregating third-party financial data from exchanges, brokers, and news sources into proprietary managed databases, combined with AI-powered analytics and workflow solutions for portfolio analysis, risk management, and reporting.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include institutional asset managers, wealth managers, asset owners, hedge funds, private equity and venture capital professionals, investment bankers, sell-side research analysts, and corporate users. Buy-side clients represent approximately 82% of organic ASV, while sell-side clients represent 18%. The company serves the global investment community across research, portfolio construction, trade execution, performance measurement, risk management, and reporting workflows.
categories.geographic_coverage: FactSet operates in 35 offices across 20 countries. The Americas segment includes offices in nine U.S. states (headquarters in Norwalk, Connecticut), Brazil, and Canada. EMEA operates in Bulgaria, England, France, Germany, Italy, Ireland, Latvia, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, and UAE. Asia Pacific operates in Australia, China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Philippines, and Singapore. Approximately 81% of employees are located outside the U.S., with significant centers of excellence in India and Philippines.
categories.supply_chain_position: FactSet operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the financial services supply chain. The company aggregates third-party financial data and content from multiple suppliers, exchanges, and brokers, then processes and delivers this data through its platform to end-user investment professionals. The CUSIP Global Services business operates as a critical infrastructure provider, issuing security identifiers used throughout the industry's front, middle, and back-office functions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: FactSet's strategic priorities focus on three core pillars: (1) expanding data offerings including industry-specific, real-time market, fund, and sustainable finance data for AI applications; (2) embedding deeper in client workflows through front-office expansion, advisor desktop expansion, and next-generation automation in research and financial modeling; (3) innovating with AI through its FactSet AI Blueprint, including AI-powered portfolio commentary, earnings call analysis, and natural language data queries. The company invests significantly in R&D for product development and technology modernization.
categories.revenue_model: FactSet generates revenues primarily through subscriptions to multi-asset class data and solutions, representing the majority of revenues. The company also generates revenues from professional services (project-based consulting and implementation services), data feeds, APIs, and managed services. Revenues are recognized based on subscription access over contractual terms. As of August 31, 2024, annual subscription value (ASV) retention exceeded 95%, indicating strong recurring revenue characteristics.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FactSet competes in the financial information services industry with both large, well-capitalized competitors and smaller niche firms. Major competitors include Bloomberg L.P., S&P's Market Intelligence division, and LSEG's Data & Analytics division (formerly Refinitiv). Other competitors include BlackRock Aladdin, MSCI Inc., and Morningstar Inc. FactSet believes it has high barriers to entry due to extensive data offerings, deep client workflow integration, and the difficulty of replicating its comprehensive data ecosystem.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: FactSet is a large-cap company with fiscal 2024 revenues of $2,203.1 million (5.6% growth) and net income of $537.1 million (14.7% growth). The company had 8,217 clients and 216,381 users as of August 31, 2024. Organic ASV plus Professional Services grew 4.8% to $2,272.8 million. The company generated free cash flow of $614.7 million in fiscal 2024 and returned $385.9 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Market capitalization was approximately $17.6 billion as of February 29, 2024.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FactSet differentiates through its comprehensive, connected data platform that spans the entire investment lifecycle with sophisticated analytics and flexible technology. Key differentiators include: (1) breadth and depth of multi-asset class data with high barriers to entry; (2) deep integration into client workflows across front, middle, and back-office functions; (3) open and flexible technology architecture enabling customization and API access; (4) pragmatic AI approach enhancing rather than replacing workflows; (5) critical role in capital markets through CUSIP identifier services; (6) high customer retention (>95% ASV retention) indicating strong customer stickiness and value delivery.
